beats.beat: The company's product line falls into four categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). These are used across multiple industries — plastics, paints, cosmetics, construction, and water treatment.

Sales are executed through a long-term arrangement with 20 Microns Limited, the corporate promoter, which markets and sells the company's products through its network. This is the company's primary route to market.

Customer concentration is moderate: the top ten customers accounted for 59%, 57%, and 59% of revenue in FY2015, FY2016, and FY2017 respectively. No long-term agreements exist with customers or raw-material suppliers; business is governed by purchase orders.
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka, reporting exports of ₹106.82 crore over the past five years. It also highlights import substitution as a competitive strength.

beats.beat: The company turned profitable only from fiscal 2015 onwards. After losses of ₹27.40 lakh in FY2013 and ₹12.17 lakh in FY2014, it posted a profit after tax of ₹149.58 lakh in FY2015. PAT continued to grow to ₹174.82 lakh in FY2016 before dipping to ₹90.18 lakh in FY2017. For the six months ended September 2017, PAT was ₹132.75 lakh.
Earnings per share (basic) mirrored the profit pattern: negative ₹0.45 in FY2013, ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹2.43 in FY2016, ₹1.46 in FY2017, and ₹1.48 for the six months ended September 2017.

Operating cash flows have been volatile. Net cash from operations was ₹200.97 lakh in FY2013, turned negative to ₹349.75 lakh in FY2014, then swung to positive ₹802.59 lakh in FY2015, ₹422.36 lakh in FY2016, fell to ₹127.73 lakh in FY2017, and was ₹124.86 lakh for the six months ended September 2017. The company acknowledges that sustained negative cash flows could impact growth.
Total assets have grown from ₹2,679.38 lakh in FY2013 to ₹3,424.96 lakh as of September 2017. The company had contingent liabilities of ₹29.11 lakh as of September 30, 2017.

beats.beat: The company is controlled by four promoters: three individuals — Chandresh S. Parikh, Atil C. Parikh, and Rajesh C. Parikh — and the corporate entity 20 Microns Limited. Together, they hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital. The promoter group (excluding promoters) holds the remaining 0.24% (21,510 shares).

The company has entered into related party transactions in each of the last five financial years and the six months ended September 2017, as per Accounting Standard 18. The filing states that such transactions may continue and could adversely affect financial condition.

The company does not own the premises for two of its manufacturing facilities (Plot 347, GIDC Waghodia, Gujarat and Plot 104/3, Thenkasi Road, Tamil Nadu) and its administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur. It also lacks statutory licenses for its facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, and has had instances of non-filing/delays with the Registrar of Companies.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals market (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at around ₹1,000 billion in fiscal 2017, growing at a 10-12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017. CRISIL Research forecasts acceleration to 12-14% CAGR going forward.

Key demand drivers include rising GDP, urbanisation (urban population expected to reach 36% by 2020), growth in end-use sectors like paints, plastics, construction, and cosmetics, and favourable government policies such as 100% FDI allowance and the Draft National Chemical Policy.

The industry is highly fragmented: small and medium enterprises hold 70-75% market share. Only a few Indian players can compete with global giants on product development and innovation. The company positions itself on product innovation and R&D.

Headwinds include a sustained import surplus (imports CAGR 6.4% vs exports CAGR 6% over 2012-2017), strict EU regulations (REACH) affecting exports, and the transitional impact of GST, effective July 1, 2017.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals processes and sells specialty chemicals — functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft and hard minerals. It operates through a long-term marketing arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, which holds 99.76% of the company's pre-issue equity.

The company is raising capital through a fresh issue (no offer-for-sale component) to fund a new manufacturing facility in Waghodia, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes. The issue will list on NSE EMERGE, the SME platform.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who 20 Microns Nano Minerals is, what it does, and what the IPO is about.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares; there is no offer for sale. The company intends to use the proceeds primarily to fund capital expenditure for setting up a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat. A portion is allocated to general corporate purposes.
A secondary objective is to create a public trading market for the shares by listing on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE), enhancing visibility and brand.
The book-running lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited. The registrar to the issue is Link Intime India Private Limited.

beats.beat: 1. No long-term agreements with customers or raw material suppliers. Sales and procurement are governed by purchase orders, which can be terminated or renegotiated anytime, exposing the company to volume and price volatility.
2. Past negative cash flows and volatility. Operating cash flow was negative in FY2014 (-₹349.75 lakh) and has been inconsistent, which could constrain growth and debt servicing.
3. Missing statutory licenses for one manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia. The company cannot assure it will not be penalized, which could disrupt operations.
4. Related party transactions. The company has historically transacted with promoters and group companies, and may continue to do so, raising conflict-of-interest concerns.
5. Legal proceedings. The company, its promoters, group companies, and directors are parties to certain legal proceedings. An adverse outcome could materially affect finances.
